q: 1. The property of the ingredients to separate from each other while placing the concrete is called ...........
explain: Segregation is the separation of constituent materials of concrete, usually resulting in the coarse aggregate settling or separating from the matrix.

q: 2. In a combined footing for two columns carrying unequal loads, the maximum hogging bending moment will occur ...........
explain: In combined footings, the shear force diagram typically crosses zero (maximum moment) near the heavier load point.

q: 3. To ensure uniform pressure distribution, the thickness of the foundation, is ...........
explain: Varying the thickness (as in sloped or stepped footings) helps distribute the stiffness and pressure more effectively.

q: 4. As per I.S. 456: 2000, the vertical deflection limits in a cantilever beam may generally be assumed to be satisfied provided that (span/depth) ratio does not exceed ...........
explain: To control deflection, IS 456 specifies basic span-to-effective-depth ratios: 7 for cantilevers, 20 for simply supported, and 26 for continuous beams.

q: 5. The spacing of vertical stirrups in a rectangular beam is ............
explain: Since shear force is highest at supports, stirrups are needed most there, resulting in the minimum (closest) spacing.

q: 6. A T-beam behaves like a rectangular beam of width equal to its flange, if neutral axis
explain: When the neutral axis is within the flange, the entire compression zone is rectangular (width = Bf). Since concrete in tension is ignored, the shape of the web doesn't affect the stress calculation.

q: 7. A T-beam behaves as a rectangular beam of a width equal to its flange if its neutral axis
options: at the bottom edge of the slab
explain: If the compression zone (neutral axis) is contained entirely within the top flange, the calculation is identical to that of a rectangular beam of flange width.

q: 8. At continuous supports, the lower portion of
options: the slab experience neither the tension nor compression
explain: At supports of a continuous beam, hogging occurs. This means the top is in tension and the bottom (lower portion) is in compression.

q: 9. The maximum diameter of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. slabs is
explain: IS 456 specifies that the maximum diameter of reinforcing bars shall not exceed 1/8th of the total thickness of the slab.

q: 10. In a slab, the transverse reinforcement is provided at... to the span of the slab
explain: Transverse reinforcement is placed perpendicular (90 degrees) to the main span reinforcement.

q: 11. According to I.S.: 456-1978, the deflection of reinforced concrete slab or beam, for the purpose of design, is limited to... of span
explain: The span/250 limit is equivalent to 0.4%, but the question refers to the 1978 version where specific limits for finishes were set at 0.25% (span/400).

q: 12. In a simply supported slab, alternate bars are curtailed at
explain: In simply supported slabs, bending moment reduces towards the ends, so bars are often cranked or curtailed at L/7 from the center of the support.

q: 13. In case of two-way slab, the limiting deflection of the slab is
options: primarily a function of the long span
primarily a function of the short span
independent of long or short spans
dependent on both long and short spans
explain: Deflection control for two-way slabs is based on the shorter span because it is the stiffer direction that carries more load.

q: 14. A ribbed slab is provided where
explain: Ribbed slabs are efficient for long spans and provide voids that can be used for acoustic/thermal insulation or to hide services while maintaining a flat ceiling profile if covered.

q: 15. For a ribbed slab, the overall depth, slab, should not be less than 75 mm...
explain: To ensure lateral stability of the ribs, the depth of the rib should not exceed four times its width.

q: 16. Enlarged head of a supporting column of a flat slab, is known as
explain: The flared or enlarged top of a column in a flat slab system is technically called the column capital.

q: 17. The splicing of the reinforcement bars in R.C.C. beams can be done at a section where
options: bending moment is less than half the maximum B.M. on the beam
bending moment is more than half the maximum B.M. on the beam
explain: Splices should ideally be located away from sections of maximum stress; usually where the BM is less than 50% of the maximum BM.

q: 18. Lap splices in tension reinforcement are permitted for bars
explain: Lap splices are not recommended for bars larger than 36 mm; such bars should be welded or joined by mechanical couplers.

q: 19. The maximum horizontal distance between parallel main reinforcement in beams is
explain: The code specifies maximum spacing limits to control crack widths; for Fe415, it is typically around 180mm, falling in the 125-235 range.

q: 20. The deflection including the effects of temperature, creep and shrinkage occurring after erection of partitions and the applications of finishes should not normally exceed
options: span/250 or 20 mm whichever is less
span/350 or 20 mm whichever is less
explain: For the safety of finishes and partitions, the deflection occurring after their application is strictly limited to Span/350 or 20 mm.

q: 21. Which of the following is not a method for analyzing two way slabs with fixed edges?
explain: Hardy-Cross is a moment distribution method primarily used for continuous beams and rigid frames, not specifically for two-way slab analysis.

q: 22. The drop of a flat slab may have thickness........ more than the rest of the slab
explain: The drop panel is a thickened portion of the slab around the column designed to resist negative moments and punching shear; it typically increases slab thickness by 25% to 50%.

q: 23. Distribution reinforcement in a simply supported slab, is provided to distribute
explain: Secondary reinforcement (distribution bars) helps spread concentrated loads and controls cracking caused by temperature changes and concrete shrinkage.

q: 24. The transverse reinforcement provided at right angles to the main reinforcement
explain: Transverse reinforcement (distribution steel) performs all these functions: load spreading, temperature resistance, and shrinkage control.

q: 25. If the ratio of long and short spans of a two way slab with corners held down is r, the actual reduction of B.M. is given by
explain: Based on Marcus's method for two-way slabs, the reduction factor involves the span ratio raised to the fourth power.

q: 26. According to I.S. 456, slabs which span in two directions with corners held down, are assumed to be divided in each direction into middle strips and edge strips such that the width of the middle strip, is
options: half of the width of the slab
two-third of the width of the slab
three-fourth of the width of the slab
four-fifth of the width of the slab
explain: IS 456 defines the middle strip as the central 3/4th (75%) of the span in each direction.

q: 27. Design of a two way slab simply supported on edge and having no provision to prevent the corners from lifting is made by
explain: The Rankine-Grashoff theory is used for slabs where corners are free to lift, which assumes no torsional resistance at corners.

q: 28. The effective width of a column strip of flat slab, is
options: one-fourth the width of the panel
half the width of the panel
explain: In flat slab design, the column strip is defined as having a width equal to 50% (half) of the panel width.

q: 29. A circular slab subjected to external loading deflects to form a
explain: Due to uniform loading and radial symmetry, the elastic deflection curve of a circular plate/slab follows a paraboloid of revolution.

q: 30. A very comfortable type of stairs is
explain: Open newel stairs provide a central well for ventilation and light, making them more spacious and comfortable for users.

q: 31. For stairs spanning l meters longitudinally between supports at the bottom and of a flight carrying a load w per unit horizontal area, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is
explain: Like a simply supported beam, a longitudinally spanning stair flight experiences a maximum moment of wl²/8.

q: 32. If longitudinally spanning stairs are casted along with their landings, the maximum bending moment per metre width, is taken as
explain: Casting with landings creates partial continuity, which reduces the effective maximum bending moment to approximately wl²/10.

q: 33. The number of treads in a flight is equal to
explain: In a flight of stairs, there is always one less tread than there are risers because the top tread is often part of the landing.

q: 34. Design of R.C.C. cantilever beams, is based on the resultant force at
explain: In a cantilever beam, both the maximum bending moment and maximum shear force occur at the fixed support (the 'fixed end').
